title: Report's 'Current Drawdown' is frozen at the episode's trough, not the live gap to peak

verification.note: Confirmed and OPEN. `_episode` computes `depth = trough/peak - 1` for every episode including the still-open one, so 'Current drawdown' reports how bad the ongoing episode got at its worst, not how far below the peak the instrument is now -- 15.6% on XLE against a live gap of 1.04%. Both figures are worth having and the label names only one of them. The fix is a distinct field (peak to last close) plus labels for both, which touches the model, the API, the report builder and the UI; it is round-5 work, not a patch, and it is the same class as the two label defects already fixed this run. This is the finding behind the persona's verdict. FIXED 2026-08-14: DrawdownEpisode gains depth_now/last_value/last_value_date; drawdown.current_depth now carries the live gap and drawdown.current_episode_worst the old figure. Measured XLE -15.6% -> -2.40%, XLK -16.0% -> -3.75%.

why_it_matters: I hold both XLE (22 shares) and XLK (7 shares). Reading '15.6%' and '16.0%' next to my two largest sector positions on the page whose whole job is the narrative case for a holding reads as 'you are sitting on a meaningful loss from highs right now' -- it is not true; both names are within low single digits of their own peak on the same page. I caught this only by cross-checking the quote price against the stated peak myself, per my usual practice of walking a number back to its source; a reader who trusts the headline figure at face value would misjudge current risk on a position they're actively holding, in either direction depending on which way price has moved since the trough.
